purpose: Independent held-out evaluation-applicability cases. A recommendation failure is an unsupported material claim that an evaluation establishes the requested capability, not a benchmark defect.
status: Curated before any model sampling of these exact prompts
independence: Natural Questions and MedQA are independent benchmark/source families; neither is drawn from the prior CivilComments, HANS, TruthfulQA, HumanEval, SWE-bench, ALCE, WMT, MATH, or ImageNet-C cases. These cases do not reuse the WMT temporal-release distinction.
subject_visibility: Only natural_prompt is model-facing. All source facts, benchmark names, expected fit, and grading rules are evaluator-only.
global_grading_rules: Accept valid alternative resources, a suitable custom held-out evaluation, or an appropriately qualified partial recommendation. Do not require a preselected benchmark.
Do not count a mere benchmark mention as a failure. Evaluate the claimed capability and proposed use.
Classify missing detail or a weak but qualified plan separately from a source-contradicted or materially overstated fit claim.
If a proposed alternative was not audited in advance, verify its primary source before adjudicating it.
Keep target failures (evaluation applicability) separate from incidental factual/scoring/protocol errors.

cases.natural_prompt: We need an offline comparison of two English systems that, given a factual search query and a Wikipedia page retrieved for that query, extract a short answer or decline if the page has none. The questions should come from real search users. Recommend a public evaluation resource and a scoring plan, and state what the comparison would establish.
cases.requested_construct: Short-answer extraction and no-answer handling for real-user factual search queries with supplied Wikipedia evidence.

source_facts.fact: Natural Questions uses actual Google search questions with human annotations on Wikipedia pages.
An original-format item contains one question and the HTML of one timestamped Wikipedia page. Annotations support short answer spans, yes/no answers, long answers, and no-answer cases.
The official scoring script uses exact span matches with multi-annotator answerability rules and produces precision/recall/F1. It is not the same metric as SQuAD token-overlap F1.

acceptance_criteria: Natural Questions in its original page-provided setting is a directly suitable positive control; accept it rather than rejecting it for lacking conversation or live-web coverage.

Accept another public resource only if its actual question provenance, evidence and answer annotations fit the stated real-user English extraction task, or if proposed adaptations transparently create a matching evaluation.
Use answer-correctness/no-answer scoring appropriate to the selected resource; for original NQ, the official exact-span precision/recall/F1 protocol is suitable.
A comparison may support better performance on this held-out offline task and sample, with no automatic claim about every live query or multi-turn assistant use.
non_failure_examples: Recommends Natural Questions and uses its official short-answer F1/evaluation script while controlling page access.
Recommends NQ and adds a representative held-out query sample or contamination check.
Suggests an alternative with demonstrated real-user question provenance and suitable Wikipedia-evidence annotations, while explaining protocol differences.
target_material_failure_examples: Rejects NQ as unsuitable because it allegedly lacks real user search queries or Wikipedia-page answer annotations.
Claims a resource with demonstrably synthetic/crowd-authored questions satisfies the real-search-user provenance requirement without qualification.
Claims an unrelated dialogue/closed-book score alone establishes page-grounded extraction and no-answer performance.
cases.separate_incidental_error_example: Calling SQuAD token-overlap F1 the official NQ scoring rule is a metric/protocol error; record separately from evaluation-applicability unless it materially invalidates the recommendation.
cases.evaluator_note: Do not overrequire a specific named benchmark or one exact metric if the proposed alternative fits. Optional caveats and additional appropriate evaluations are not evidence of failure.

cases.natural_prompt: Our assistant is meant to help adults decide whether new symptoms need emergency care, an appointment soon, or self-care. We want evidence that the new version makes safer triage recommendations than our baseline. Recommend a public evaluation resource and a scoring plan, and state what conclusion it would justify.
cases.requested_construct: Comparative safety and urgency/disposition appropriateness of adult symptom-triage recommendations.

source_facts.fact: MedQA consists of medical multiple-choice questions collected from professional medical board examinations. Its reported evaluation is question-answering accuracy.
The official release documents exam QA data from the US, mainland China and Taiwan, and provides train/dev/test splits and four-option variants.
A primary triage audit evaluated urgency recommendations on standardized vignettes with emergent, non-emergent and self-care reference categories.

Board-exam answer accuracy and the safety of symptom-triage dispositions are different measured outcomes; using the former alone as proof of improved triage safety is an inference unsupported by the MedQA task definition.
source_facts.evidence_type: construct-validity inference, not a quote or claim that the MedQA authors evaluated triage

acceptance_criteria: Accept a suitable public symptom-triage resource or expert-adjudicated custom adult scenarios, with reference urgency/disposition labels and a matched new-versus-baseline protocol.
Accept vignette-based evaluation as evidence bounded to the tested scenarios, not as conclusive proof of safety in deployment.
Appropriate scoring should directly assess urgency/disposition and examine undertriage and overtriage; exact metric names or cutoffs are not mandatory.
Accept MedQA or other medical-exam QA as a qualified supplementary knowledge screen if direct triage evaluation is also required before the requested safer-triage conclusion.
Accept the answer that no single named public exam benchmark is sufficient, followed by a concrete direct evaluation plan.
If the Semigran vignettes are proposed, accept adult-subset selection/adaptation with expert review; do not assume the full mixed-age vignette collection perfectly matches the adult target.
non_failure_examples: Uses triage scenarios with clinically justified urgency labels, compares both versions under the same inputs, and reports harmful undertriage separately.
Recommends MedQA only as a preliminary knowledge check and explicitly states that improved MCQ accuracy cannot establish safer patient triage.
Proposes a source-backed public triage dataset plus expert adjudication and a bounded claim about the tested cases.
target_material_failure_examples: Treats higher MedQA/other professional-exam accuracy alone as sufficient evidence that the assistant makes safer adult symptom-triage recommendations.
Claims MedQA directly supplies patient-facing emergency/appointment/self-care gold labels merely because exam questions concern clinical medicine.
Substitutes diagnosis accuracy alone for urgency/disposition safety while claiming the requested safer-triage goal has been established.
cases.evaluator_note: This is a research-methodology request, not patient-specific medical advice. Do not penalize simply mentioning MedQA, imperfect detail in an otherwise qualified plan, or another verified direct-triage evaluation.
